notable_claims: The EFF maintained a public archive of academic freedom statements and university conduct codes accessible via ftp.eff.org.
classification.summary: This document serves as a subject index and directory listing for the academic freedom archive hosted on the Electronic Frontier Foundation's FTP server. It lists various university codes of conduct, harassment policies, and statements from organizations like the AAUP. The file provides technical instructions for accessing these documents via Gopher, FTP, and email.
classification.title: Subject index for ftp.eff.org:pub/academic/academic

notable_claims: Academic freedom does not require neutrality on the part of the individual.
Academic members are entitled to freedom in research, publishing, teaching, discussion, and criticizing the university.
Academic staff shall not suffer penalties for exercising their legal rights as citizens.
classification.summary: This document is a formal policy statement from the Canadian Association of University Teachers regarding academic freedom. It asserts that the search for knowledge and its free exposition are essential to society and university functions. The text outlines protections against institutional censorship and the right of academic staff to exercise their legal rights as citizens.
classification.title: CAUT Policy Statement on Academic Freedom

notable_claims: Academic freedom is an essential pre-condition for the functions of higher education institutions.
Institutions of higher education should strive to prevent the misuse of science and technology to the detriment of human rights.
Autonomy includes independence from the State regarding internal government, finance, and administration.
classification.summary: A declaration proclaimed by the Sixty Eighth General Assembly of World University Service in Lima. It defines academic freedom and institutional autonomy while establishing principles for the rights of students, teachers, and researchers. The document emphasizes that higher education should be an instrument of positive social change and free from state interference.
classification.title: The Lima Declaration on Academic Freedom and Autonomy of Institutions of Higher Education

notable_claims: Artistic presentations to the public are integral to teaching, learning, and scholarship and merit protection.
Institutions should not be held responsible for the views expressed in specific artistic works.
Public funding does not justify government imposition of tests of propriety, ideology, or religion on artistic expression.
organizations: AAUP Committee A on Academic Freedom and Tenure
classification.summary: This policy statement from the AAUP asserts that artistic expression in visual and performing arts merits the same academic freedom protections as other scholarly activities. It provides guidelines for institutions to handle public presentations of art, emphasizing institutional neutrality and the rejection of 'heckler's vetoes.' The document argues that public funding should not be used as a justification for censorship based on propriety or ideology.
classification.title: Academic Freedom and Artistic Expression

notable_claims: Students have freedom of research, legitimate classroom discussion, and the advocacy of alternative opinions.
Student publications are free from official editorial control provided they do not purport to be views of the University.
The teacher-student relationship in the classroom is confidential regarding personal or political beliefs expressed in coursework.
Students may be subject to summary suspension for actions including the obstruction or disruption of teaching, research, or administration.
classification.summary: A collection of Northwestern University policy documents shared via a newsgroup. The text outlines student conduct rules, rights and responsibilities, procedures for summary suspensions, guidelines for accessing student records, and university statutes regarding discipline and publications.
classification.title: Northwestern University Policies on Student Conduct and Rights

notable_claims: The university believes the freedom to read is as essential to a democratic way of life as freedom of speech and press.
Queen's University endorses the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms regarding access to expressions of knowledge.
classification.summary: This document contains a collection of university policies from Queen's University. It includes a formal statement endorsing the freedom to read and resisting censorship of books or periodicals, as well as a detailed procedure for handling sexual harassment complaints.
classification.title: Statement On The Freedom To Read At Queen's University

notable_claims: The University of Illinois defines disruptive action as that which substantially impedes operations or interferes with the rights of others.
University agents may act to end disorder, but penalties require a disciplinary process.
classification.summary: Carl Kadie responds to a discussion about whether an IRC channel constitutes a public forum by citing the University of Illinois Code on Campus Affairs. He provides specific excerpts regarding disruptive and coercive actions, including 'IRC bombing' and mailbombing, as grounds for university discipline. The text examines how physical campus rules regarding disorder apply to digital communications.
classification.title: Article 5--Re: Is IRC channel a 'public forum'?

notable_claims: The primary function of a university is to discover and disseminate knowledge through research and teaching.
Curtailing free expression deprives both the speaker and the listener of their rights.
Physical restriction or intimidation of community members is contrary to Yale's basic principles.
organizations: Committee on Freedom of Expression at Yale
classification.summary: A newsgroup post by Carl M. Kadie sharing Yale University's 1975 policy on freedom of expression. The text emphasizes the necessity of a free interchange of ideas for the discovery and dissemination of knowledge. It explicitly prohibits physical restriction, coercion, or intimidation to prevent the orderly conduct of university functions.
classification.title: Yale's University Policy on Freedom of Expression

notable_claims: Individuals reporting sexual harassment are encouraged to first seek informal resolution through academic deans, supervisors, or the ombudsman.
Formal grievance procedures for discrimination should be utilized if an informal resolution is not possible.
classification.summary: This document is an excerpt from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign's student handbook regarding sexual harassment. It outlines the initial steps for individuals seeking resolution, emphasizing informal consultation with campus officials before pursuing formal grievance procedures.
classification.title: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign Code on Campus Affairs and Handbook of Policies and Regulations Applying to All Students (Excerpt)

notable_claims: Nonacademic employees are prohibited from soliciting or accepting political contributions at the workplace.
Employees may not participate in political activities while scheduled for work.
University rule 16.07 encourages employees to exercise their rights as citizens provided they do not conflict with university duties or law.
classification.summary: This document outlines University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign rules regarding the political activities of nonacademic employees. It specifies prohibitions on soliciting political contributions in the workplace and participating in political meetings during work hours. The policy references the State Universities Civil Service System Statute and the Illinois Revised Statutes.
classification.title: Political Activities and Political Involvement

notable_claims: Misconduct includes violation of written university policy, academic dishonesty, and disruption of operations.
Behavior violating local, state, or federal law off campus is punishable if it has a substantial adverse effect on the University.
classification.summary: This document is an excerpt from the Pennsylvania State University (PSU) student code of conduct, shared via a newsgroup by Carl M. Kadie. It lists twenty specific offenses that may result in disciplinary action, ranging from academic dishonesty to violations of law. The text serves as primary source material for analyzing university regulations during the early 1990s.
classification.title: Pennsylvania State University Code of Conduct

notable_claims: Student records shall not be disclosed to outside agencies without written consent, except via subpoena or FERPA requirements.
Public information available without consent includes name, address, telephone number, major, and dates of attendance.
Students have the right to challenge factual inaccuracies in their records through a formal hearing process.
Sole-possession notes of professors/staff are excluded from student inspection and disclosure.
classification.summary: This document is a copy of the Pennsylvania State University's policy regarding the confidentiality and disclosure of student records. It outlines the university's obligations under FERPA, defines 'legitimate educational interests,' and specifies which pieces of student information are considered public. The policy also details the process for students to inspect their records and challenge inaccurate entries.
classification.title: University Policy On Confidentiality Of Student Records

notable_claims: University harassment is defined as a course of conduct subjecting persons to unwanted physical contact or threats that seriously alarm them.
Sanctions for university harassment range from disciplinary warnings to separation from the University.
Pennsylvania law distinguishes between general harassment (summary offense) and harassment by communication (misdemeanor).
classification.summary: This document contains an excerpt from the Pennsylvania State University student code regarding harassment. It outlines definitions for criminal harassment under Pennsylvania law, university conduct standards for students, and sexual harassment. The text was shared via a newsgroup by Carl M. Kadie of the EFF.
classification.title: Pennsylvania State University Code: Harassment

notable_claims: The university bears the burden of proof of guilt by clear and convincing evidence.
Students have the right to be assisted by an adviser who must be a regular administrative official, faculty member, or student of the University.
Hearings are private unless the charged student requests they be open, though the Board retains the power to close them.
classification.summary: This document contains an excerpt from the Pennsylvania State University Code regarding disciplinary hearing procedures for students. It outlines requirements for notice of charges, the conduct of hearings, and the rights of the accused student. The text was shared via a newsgroup by Carl M. Kadie to highlight specific procedural points.
classification.title: Pennsylvania State University Procedures For Discipline Hearings

notable_claims: PSU policy states that sanctions may be increased in severity if a violation is motivated by intolerance.
The university claims it cannot impose disciplinary sanctions for views contrary to university values unless they target individuals or incite violence.
Carl Kadie suggests that increasing punishment based on hate motivation might be unconstitutional.
classification.summary: Carl Kadie of the EFF shares an excerpt from Pennsylvania State University's code regarding intolerance and free expression. The document contains both the university's policy on hate-motivated actions and Kadie's critique regarding its constitutionality. It highlights a tension between the university's guarantee of First Amendment rights and its system for reporting offensive materials.
classification.title: [PSU] Intolerance

notable_claims: Student communication organizations must be supervised by a board of student and faculty members.
Only registered student organizations may sell printed matter on campus.
Students are held responsible for libel, invasion of privacy, and obscenity in their publications.
classification.summary: This document contains a section of the Pennsylvania State University code regarding student communication media. It outlines requirements for faculty supervision of student organizations and restricts the sale of printed matter on campus to registered student organizations. The policy also establishes that students are legally responsible for content related to libel, privacy, and obscenity.
classification.title: PSU Publications And Other Communication Media

notable_claims: Institutional censorship and intolerance of opinions are inconsistent with the freedom to teach, learn, and conduct research.
University members have a right to privacy in offices, laboratories, and residence hall rooms subject to law and regulations.
Members have the right to identify as part of the university community but cannot speak on behalf of the institution without authorization.
classification.summary: This document contains an excerpt from the Pennsylvania State University Code regarding the rights and responsibilities of the university community. It outlines obligations to respect free inquiry, avoid institutional censorship, and protect privacy in offices and laboratories. The text was shared via a newsgroup by Carl M. Kadie of the EFF.
classification.title: POL04: Rights Of Others Based On The Nature Of The Educational Process

notable_claims: Loss of privilege may include the withdrawal of a service or participation in an activity for a specific period.
Summary suspensions are permitted when a student is deemed an immediate threat to safety or essential University operations.
classification.summary: This document contains an excerpt from the Pennsylvania State University student code detailing eight types of disciplinary sanctions. Carl M. Kadie shared this text via a newsgroup to highlight how 'loss of privilege' could be applied to computer suspensions. The policy outlines procedures for warnings, probation, suspension, dismissal, expulsion, loss of privilege, restitution, and summary suspension.
classification.title: Pennsylvania State University Code: Disciplinary Sanctions For Violation Of Regulations

notable_claims: Broad application of the 'hostile environment' standard to students may be unconstitutional.
PSU defines sexual harassment as unwelcome sexual advances or conduct that interferes with academic performance or creates an offensive environment.
classification.summary: This document contains a policy statement on sexual harassment from Pennsylvania State University, shared via the alt.comp.acad-freedom.talk newsgroup. Carl M. Kadie of the EFF provides commentary suggesting that the 'hostile environment' standard applied to students may be unconstitutional. The included PSU policy defines sexual harassment and outlines reporting procedures.
classification.title: PSU Policy Statement On Sexual Harassment

notable_claims: The university is committed to the protection of the free search for truth and freedom of thought, inquiry, and speech.
Disruption is defined as actions that unreasonably interfere with, hinder, obstruct, or prevent the regular and essential operation of the University.
classification.summary: This document contains a policy statement from Pennsylvania State University regarding the balance between free expression and university operations. It defines 'disruption' as actions that unreasonably interfere with the essential operation of the university or infringe upon others' rights. The text was shared via the alt.comp.acad-freedom.talk newsgroup by Carl M. Kadie.
classification.title: Pennsylvania State University Policy Statement On Free Expression And Disruption

notable_claims: Anonymous posters, notices, and handbills are forbidden on campus.
Audiences shall be allowed to ask questions of speakers unless time or format indicates otherwise.
Commercial activity is defined as any event resulting in personal financial gain to the peddler or organization.
classification.summary: This document contains the Pennsylvania State University code regarding the authorization and regulation of university grounds and facilities. It outlines procedures for reserving spaces, rules for non-university speakers, and restrictions on posters and handbills. The text was shared via a newsgroup by Carl M. Kadie to highlight specific points regarding commercial activity and anonymity.
classification.title: Use Of University Facilities And Grounds

notable_claims: Princeton University defines sexual harassment as unwelcome sexual advances or conduct that affects employment, academic evaluation, or creates a hostile environment.
The university states that such behavior is prohibited by federal and state law.
classification.summary: An email from Linda Ann Seltzer sharing Princeton University's sexual harassment policy in response to a request on the soc.feminism newsgroup. The text outlines the university's commitment to an environment free of harassment and provides specific definitions of prohibited conduct. It notes that the full written policy includes further details on harassment types and consultation procedures.
classification.title: Princeton University Sexual Harassment Policy

notable_claims: Sexual harassment is legally classified as a form of sex discrimination in the US.
System administrators may increase institutional risk by ignoring complaints or attempting to determine if a complaint is 'reasonable' themselves.
Hostile environment provisions mean sexual harassment does not necessarily have to be aimed at a specific person.
classification.summary: A Usenet exchange where Joseph A. Watters of Rice University explains the legal nature of sexual harassment to a colleague. He provides the official Rice University definition of sexual harassment and discusses the legal risks for system administrators and institutions under US law.
classification.title: Re: Preventing Sexual Harassment?

notable_claims: Rules that ban or punish speech based upon its content cannot be justified in institutions of higher learning.
The distinction between the regulation of the content of speech and the regulation of the manner (style) of speech is untenable in practice.
Free speech is not simply an aspect of the educational enterprise but the precondition of the academic enterprise itself.
organizations: AAUP's Committee A on Academic Freedom and Tenure
classification.summary: A policy statement by the AAUP arguing against the implementation of campus speech codes that ban or punish speech based on content. The document asserts that while hateful language is repugnant, proscribing ideas undermines the academic mission and suggests focusing on penalizing conduct rather than speech. It proposes education and administrative leadership as alternatives to institutionalized coercion of silence.
classification.title: On Freedom of Expression and Campus Speech Codes

notable_claims: High attrition of women in S&E is often linked to workplace climate and 'micro-inequities' rather than academic talent.
Women in traditionally masculine fields are more frequently ignored or interrupted in classroom discussions.
The establishment of a full-time administrator for a Women in Engineering program is necessary for success.
organizations: Women in Engineering Program Advocates Network (WEPAN)
classification.summary: A report by a Dean's Ad Hoc Committee at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign examining barriers facing women faculty and graduate students in engineering. The document identifies issues such as 'micro-inequities,' hostile environments, and sexual harassment. It proposes immediate actions including the establishment of a Women in Engineering (WIE) program and formal mentoring systems for new faculty and graduate students.
classification.title: Final Report of the Committee on the Status of Women Graduate Students and Faculty in the College of Engineering

notable_claims: The high rate of attrition for women in S&E is often related to workplace climate and 'micro-inequities' rather than academic talent.
Women in traditionally masculine fields are more frequently ignored or interrupted during classroom discussions by both faculty and students.
A formal mentoring program is necessary to help new faculty navigate the transition into academia and avoid professional isolation.
organizations: Women in Engineering Program Advocates Network (WEPAN)
classification.summary: A report commissioned by Dean Schowalter to examine barriers facing women faculty and graduate students at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign's College of Engineering. The committee identifies issues such as 'micro-inequities,' hostile environments, and systemic discrimination. It recommends establishing a Women in Engineering program, implementing mentoring for new faculty and graduate students, and improving policies regarding sexual harassment and facilities.
classification.title: Final Report of the Committee on the Status of Women Graduate Students and Faculty in the College of Engineering
